research_objects.summary: Bryan directs the Build Log to separate completed committed work from a single living Next Edge horizon and to preserve a deliberately open X factor.
The direct-asset WWW runtime renders one Next Edge above newest-first completed Build Log entries and reads the horizon from a machine-readable JSON artifact.
The Turtle Terraria desktop navigation rail is constrained to the viewport so it remains sticky, with internal overflow only when its contents exceed available height.

Can the project synthesize a useful horizon from repo, D1, R2, project context, ontology, observations, failures, and an X factor without reducing inquiry to backlog automation or granting machine suggestions authority?

ctc_tags.rationale: The horizon architecture originates in the human researcher's own question about what should tug the project forward next.
The Next Edge is explicitly designed to preserve a question that sustains inquiry rather than a predetermined task.

ctc_tags.domain: Technology as Tool to Think With
ctc_tags.rationale: The public interface makes the project's evolving horizon visible and manipulable as an object for reflection rather than hiding it in a private backlog.
The change emerged from reflection on the difference between already-completed work and genuinely open inquiry after observing the live Build Log.
The changed public artifact demonstrates the revised research-process model while remaining system-research evidence, not student assessment evidence.
Human direction changed the machine-assisted implementation, and the resulting horizon remains visibly open to subsequent human replacement or revision.

ontology_tags.rationale: The Next Edge preserves multiple possible directions without collapsing them into one predetermined outcome.
The horizon becomes a persistent project artifact carried between build cycles instead of disappearing with each conversation.
The concept emerged through human observation and machine-assisted design, while final direction remains attributable to the human researcher.
A future synthesizer must combine heterogeneous signals without erasing where they came from or their evidentiary status.
Each completed build changes the evidence available for generating the next question, creating a recursive build-observe-question cycle.

uncaptured_observations.text: It is not yet known whether the quality described as 'I would keep working on this if I did not have to go to bed' can be operationalized without sterilizing the very unpredictability that makes the Next Edge useful.
